machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory
scope: Short native 1024x1024 transformer optimization loop using one or two prefixes of the canonical 40-step schedule

fixture.semantics: Step 1 performs full joint attention and extracts the prompt K/V cache. Step 2 exercises target-only attention with that cached prefix. Both are the first steps of the normal 40-step schedule.

baseline_two_query_attention.interpretation: The cached prompt prefix does not materially reduce the 4096-token quadratic attention work; per-step transformer compute is the dominant target.

rejected_shared_kv8.design: Four SIMD groups shared an eight-key FP32 threadgroup tile, loading K/V once for eight queries while preserving each two-query online-softmax calculation.
rejected_shared_kv8.reason: Two barriers per eight-key tile and threadgroup synchronization outweighed the reduced device reads. The prototype was removed.

accepted_four_query.design: One 32-lane SIMD group owns four queries of one head, reusing every K/V vector across four independent online softmax states without barriers.
accepted_four_query.decision: Use four queries per SIMD group only at 1024px until superseded there by Flash Attention; retain two queries at 256px and 512px.

rejected_fp16_kv_scalar.design: Retain scalar four-query online attention but store K/V in FP16.
rejected_fp16_kv_scalar.reason: Only 3-3.5% faster in the favorable run, with no cached win in a hotter repeat. Flash Attention captures FP16 bandwidth with an order-of-magnitude kernel gain.

rejected_scalar_eight_query.design: One SIMD group retains eight independent scalar online-softmax states to maximize K/V reuse.

rejected_fast_mask.design: Hoist the fact that every image query can attend every valid key, removing image-ID comparisons from the scalar inner loop.
rejected_fast_mask.reason: The exact 1.7% full-step win is too small to retain beside the much faster flash path.

accepted_flash128_fp16_kv.design: Fixed 32-head, dimension-128 Flash Attention with eight queries, 64 keys per tile, four SIMD groups, FP16 matrix operands, and FP32 score/softmax/output accumulation.
accepted_flash128_fp16_kv.reference: llama.cpp Metal Flash Attention structure at commit 2f3fd0252 (MIT), specialized without its GGML runtime or generic template machinery.
accepted_flash128_fp16_kv.decision: Use Flash Attention at 256px and 1024px after independent production gates. Keep the exact two-query kernel at 512px until that shape is measured.

integrated_four_query_1024.accuracy: The isolated production-shape attention outputs are bit-exact to the scalar reference (nRMSE 0). The unchanged 256px two-step trajectory passes official latent gates at 0.000906469 and 0.00130081 nRMSE.

integrated_flash128_1024.accuracy: The isolated production-shape prefill and cached operators pass a 0.001 nRMSE gate against scalar FP32. No official complete 1024 trajectory oracle exists yet. The unchanged 256px two-step path passes its official latent gates at 0.000906469 and 0.00130081 nRMSE.

limitations: One-step timings intentionally exclude text encoding, VAE decoding, and image output.
GPU frequency varies between runs, so acceptance requires both dispatch-order measurements and the integrated repeat rather than a single percentage.
This optimization improves full transformer steps; Cache-DiT-skipped steps do not execute attention and therefore do not receive the same saving.
The 1024 Flash Attention result has isolated operator accuracy coverage but not a complete official 1024 trajectory oracle; adding that oracle remains a separate phase.
